audit.why: Levels 1-5 belong to Aatrox and the entry says so consistently. The Darkin Blade is 14s at rank 1 falling to 6s at rank 5 and Umbral Dash is 9s falling to 5s, so his trade pattern refreshes far faster than Arctic Assault's 18s or Winter's Wrath's 9s at rank 1. Side lane and teamfights flip to Sejuani once Glacial Prison and a tank item exist. No change needed to the shape of the lane.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2].text names Goredrinker as Aatrox's first-item spike.
audit.why: Goredrinker is not a purchasable item on 26.15 and has not been for several seasons. A named item spike a player cannot see on the shop screen destroys trust in the rest of the entry. I removed the name rather than substituting a replacement, because I cannot verify Aatrox's current first-item ordering from the kit files and will not guess it.
audit.corrected: spikes[2].text now says 'his second-item spike' and spends the reclaimed space on the Frost-into-Permafrost-into-shatter sequence, which is verifiable from Riot's text.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two decisive interactions are absent from every field. Fury of the North grants immunity to slows, and Fury of the North shatters a stunned enemy for massive magic damage. Neither is stated. Separately the entry never names Infernal Chains and calls it 'his W pull' four times without ever giving its cooldown.
audit.why: Riot's Sejuani passive text: 'Sejuani gains Frost Armor which grants Armor and Magic Resist and immunity to slows... Sejuani can damage a stunned enemy to shatter it, dealing massive magic damage.' Aatrox's Infernal Chains is his only sticking tool and its slow is switched off outright while Frost Armor holds, which changes the disengage rule from 'Q away' to 'walk away, and keep Q'. The shatter means Permafrost is not merely lost time for him — it is the largest damage instance Sejuani has, and an entry that treats her stun as pure utility undersells her whole trade. Infernal Chains is 20/18/16/14/12, the longest cooldown in his kit by a wide margin and the actual punish window the entry keeps gesturing at.
audit.corrected: Frost Armor's slow immunity and the shatter are now stated in report[5].t and late; Infernal Chains is named with its 20s rank-1 cooldown in spikes[0].text, wants.foe[2] and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns lists only World Ender and gives no number for anything.
audit.why: The entry's whole green-light system is 'is World Ender up', but it never tells the reader how long that is, and it omits the cooldown that actually decides lane trades. World Ender is 120/100/80; Infernal Chains is 20 at rank 1. A 20-second window where he cannot hold you still is a tradeable window; the entry currently hides it.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns now carries 120s for World Ender, 20s for Infernal Chains and 18s for Arctic Assault.

audit.whatIsWrong: late claims 'the 57% win rate'. MC_WR_TABLES.sejuani.aatrox is 47.74.
audit.why: The number in the prose contradicts the number the page itself renders, and it inverts the matchup's direction — 47.74 means Sejuani is losing this matchup, not winning it comfortably. I removed the figure rather than swapping in either candidate, because the audit packet reports 57.08 for the same matchup and I cannot tell which source is authoritative.
audit.corrected: The percentage claim is deleted from late; the sentence keeps its objective-fight point without a number.

audit.whatIsWrong: late attributes Sejuani's resistances to 'your armor stacking from Permafrost passive'.
audit.why: Permafrost has no passive. The armour and magic resist come from Frost Armor on Fury of the North, which only applies after she has been out of combat — a conditional the entry erases by attaching it to the wrong ability. A player who believes their armour comes from casting E will step into a fight expecting resistances they do not have.
audit.corrected: late now credits the resistances correctly and states the shatter.

edits.after: At two-plus items Frost Armor's resistances make you near-unkillable in the extended teamfights he thrives in, and his World Ender drain cannot keep pace with the CC uptime you bring. Hit him with Glacial Prison when he dives your carries, then chain Permafrost on anyone caught in the blizzard — and remember Fury of the North lets you shatter a stunned target for massive magic damage, so your own stun is your largest damage instance, not just lost time for him. Every objective fight from Baron to Dragon is a Sejuani game if you land the 1300-range R.

This is the window that drives the 57% win rate: every objective fight from Baron to Dragon is a Sejuani game if you land the R.
